StratGWAS 0.1.0
  • Reference
Performs a stratified genome-wide association study (GWAS) of a binary trait by leveraging clinical heterogeneity among cases. Cases are stratified using a secondary phenotype (e.g. age of onset, symptom severity, or recruitment definition), genetic covariance between strata is estimated, and a transformed phenotype that upweights cases with higher inferred genetic liability is constructed for GWAS. An inflation criterion quantifies the risk that a given stratification variable introduces false-positive associations, allowing risky strata to be flagged before genome-wide analysis.
